text.title: Family Size
text.declared_genre: Alternative Hip-Hop / Acoustic Folk / Spoken Word
text.declared_key: A minor, lifting toward C major in final hook
text.declared_mood: Wry, anxious, self-mocking, vulnerable → tender, defiant, quietly hopeful
text.production_notes: Fingerpicked acoustic guitar with percussive busker groove, Lo-fi hip-hop drums: soft kick, brushed snare, hand taps, Warm upright-style bass, Sparse piano after second hook, Gentle organ pad in final third, Live, imperfect, close mix, Full-stop dropouts before punchlines, Final hook adds soft harmonies while staying raw and uncluttered
text.vocal_notes: Intimate male vocal, Spoken-word rap verses with conversational phrasing, sharp pauses, dry comic timing, Soft indie-folk sung hook, Starts sardonic and nervous, becomes exposed and human, Close-mic verses, slight rasp on confession lines, occasional whispered doubles, Final section warmer and more melodic

transcription.text: If I don't think the package says new look, same price, less inside which is rude because lately I've been looking suspiciously, new look myself, I picked up a chocolate bar from the corner shop shelf and thought it'd hang on me, you used to be yourself, same wrap the same smile, same confident fun, same little promise of exactly what I want but the thing in my hand felt thin as an excuse like joy had been ordered for casual use and I laughed, then I didn't because that's been me lately, same face in the glass but the contents feel shady, same name, same coat, same jokes on repeat but I walk up the stairs and negotiate with my feet, I open a book I once would have swallowed and now page 3 has a hill to follow, I used to catch thoughts like coins from the air and I've packed down my pockets, nothing is there, maybe I'm tired, maybe I'm scared, maybe the shelf looks the same but there's less of me there and my family's size with the family gone, same little box with the old weight wrong, they kept the price but they took out the shine instead of floor to floor, or is falling the design, also who decided 27 crisps was a serving, I'd like names, there was a time I could juggle six tabs in my brain two conversations in the kettle of pain, a deadline to build a half written plan, now I lose my keys, well they're still in my hand, I read the same sentence nine times in a row, life, maybe the tenth will agree to come home, I stare at a phone with my brother man face and suddenly language that has left the place, things that were easy, now ask for the chair, emails arrive and I need medical care, a password reset feels mythic and cruel, a printer says error, and I leave the room when people say that's normal, you're just getting older, which is comforting in the way a white sock is a blank key, because I don't just miss you, I miss ease, I miss opening the door and trusting the keys, I miss being quick without making a speech, I miss feeling the answer, just slightly in reach and my family's size with the family gone, same little box with the old weight long they kept the price, the NATO got the shine, is there a floor to fall in, or is falling the design, and I know, everyone says the plan is natural, which is true, so is no do, it doesn't mean I want it, in the corners of my mind, I'm scared there's no bottom, that's the bit, not that I'm slower, not that my back now makes noises like an old ship considering prayer, not that I need the cover, but time from sitting badly, it's the wandering, is this a dip, a season, a warning, a receipt, is my brain tied, or even by degrees, that someone quietly reduced the grams of me while keeping the packaging neat, and what if I get back to this smaller version, then wake up next year, smaller again, how many losses can you call a adjustment, before the word starts looking away, I used to think aging would arrive with a bell, a dramatic little cloak, and a story to tell, but it came a small thefts, insensible shoes, a name I misplaced, the bruise I didn't choose, and I'd have a requirement three days of repair, a succumb on the floor becoming a dare, a sharp little word from someone I loved, because my patience ran out with the milk and the gloves and less, I still laugh, I'm not made of glass, I can still make the joke while I'm fitting my sense, because humor's the trolley, with the squeaking wheel, that carries the dread, to somewhere less real, but beneath all the bits in the shop floor, complaint, there's a kid in my chest saying, tell me, I ain't, being replaced by a cheap design, with smaller ideas, and a stowa mind, maybe I'm less than I was yesterday, or maybe I'm measuring roll on a terrible day, and my family's size with the family gone insane, little box with the old weight, don't they get the trance that they took out the shine, is there a floor that's falling, the doors falling, the design, maybe I'm the smaller, maybe that's true, it's all that things still hold, what they're meant to, the nature's small, but it knows how to blow, the seed looks finished, till it starts to grow, so yes, maybe there's less in the packet, maybe the label lies, maybe I need more rest now, more lists, more kindness, less pretending, I'm a warehouse with unlimited stock, but I am not empty, not yet, there's still something here worth opening, still sold at the bottom, still crumbs on the corner, still enough sweet, still make it tired, standing, catching the midnight, and saying, all right then, one more day, say, all right then, one more day,
